sources_considered.why: Primary experimental evidence of training-image reproduction.
Primary experimental evidence of substantial text extraction from contemporary language models.
Relevant privacy-preserving learning method; its guarantee must not be overstated as zero copying.
The developer acknowledges mitigation measures and disputes the representativeness of induced reproduction.

evidence_items.explanation: The study demonstrates training-image memorization and reproduction. It supports the observed tendency, but does not prove that every contemporary learning method must retain it.

evidence_items.locator: Appendix E, Verbatim Memorized Training Sequences
evidence_items.explanation: The paper documents substantial text reproduction from ChatGPT using an extraction attack. This establishes susceptibility, not the frequency of accidental copying in ordinary use or its inevitability.

evidence_items.locator: Section 6, Conclusions; guarantee defined in Section 2
evidence_items.explanation: This pre-existing method demonstrates useful image learning with formal privacy protections and bears against an unrestricted inevitability claim. Differential privacy does not guarantee that no generated image will ever resemble training material.
OpenAI describes mitigation and disputes whether induced examples represent normal use. Its statement supplies no independent measurement establishing elimination of the risk.

unresolved_gaps: The studies demonstrate susceptibility, not that useful learning necessarily retains it.
The cited extraction experiments do not establish the rate of inadvertent reproduction in ordinary use.
Privacy guarantees and mitigation claims do not establish zero substantial reproduction across the claimed scope.
